paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.

model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates the accuracy of two methods, “Vanilla CoT” and “TLDR (Ours)”, across four datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The horizontal axis displays the dataset names, listed in the order GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, represents accuracy values on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks every 20 units. For each dataset, there are two bars displayed side-by-side, with “Vanilla CoT” represented by a light yellow color and “TLDR (Ours)” represented by a dark green color. In the GSM8K dataset, the “Vanilla CoT” bar reaches approximately 89.4% accuracy, while the “TLDR (Ours)” bar extends to approximately 86.8% accuracy. The MATH500 dataset shows bars reaching approximately 42.9% and 81.5% for “Vanilla CoT” and “TLDR (Ours)” respectively. For AIME, the “Vanilla CoT” bar reaches around 1.7% accuracy, and the “TLDR (Ours)” bar extends to 89.4%. Finally, for AMC, the bar heights are approximately 81.5% for “Vanilla CoT” and 86.8% for “TLDR (Ours)”.  Above each bar, percentage changes in accuracy relative to the “Vanilla CoT” method are indicated, ranging from -1.7% to +1.6%. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining.
